'''Dimitri Manuel Mihalas''' (March 20, 1939 – November 21, 2013) was a [[laboratory]] [[fellow]] at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] in the field of [[astronomy]], [[astrophysics]], and [[Stellar atmosphere|stellar atmospheres]]. He was born in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] and was of [[Greeks|Greek]] origin.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=e-IrAQAAMAAJ&q=%22Mihalas,+Dimitri+%22+mar+1939 |title=Who's who in Frontiers of Science and Technology|year=1985|publisher=Marquis Who's Who |isbn=9780837957029}}</ref><ref name=SFobit>{{cite web|url=http://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/lanl-astrophysicist-dimitri-mihalas-dies-at/article_a1c29a93-d2df-51fe-a4aa-929a8f8bcc09.html |title=LANL astrophysicist Dimitri Mihalas dies at 74 |publisher=The Santa Fe New Mexican |date=2013-05-24 |accessdate=2013-11-29}}</ref>

Mihalas obtained his [[bachelor's degree]] in [[physics]], [[mathematics]], and [[astronomy]] from the [[University of California]], [[Los Angeles]], in 1959. In one year, he received his master's degree from [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1960. He completed his PhD degree in three years in 1963 in physics and astronomy, also from [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=AAS>{{cite journal|title=Dimitri M. Mihalas (1939 - 2013)|journal=Bulletin of the American Astronomical Society|url=https://baas.aas.org/pub/dimitri-m-mihalas-1939-2013/release/1|language=en|date=2013|volume=45 |issue=1 |last1=Cheng |first1=Baolian |last2=Castor |first2=John |last3=Stone |first3=Jim }}</ref>

At a very early age of 42, he became a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=AAS/>

Besides a large number of  scientific papers, mostly related to radiative transfer, Mihalas authored reference books such as "Stellar Atmospheres".<ref name=AAS/>

Mihalas had [[bipolar disorder]]. He wrote a number of essays and books on the problem.<ref name=SFobit/><ref name=AAS/>
